2_Introduction: PSCs based on additives achieved a PCE of 16.8841%, with a VOC of 1.138 V, FF of 70.0905%, and JSC of 21.168 mA/cm². The perovskite precursor solution was prepared with a concentration of 1.73 mol/L using PbI2 and MAI dissolved in a mixed DMF/DMSO solvent. The perovskite precursor solutions were spin-coated on the substrates at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. To promote better film morphology, 220 µL of antisolvent was added at last 6 s in the latter spin-coating step. After spin-coating, the films were annealed on the hot plate at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as MAPbI₃ with a nominal ABX₃ stoichiometry (A = CH₃NH₃⁺, B = Pb²⁺, X = I⁻), exhibits intrinsic thermodynamic instability arising from low Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.91), high ion migration propensity—particularly of MA⁺ and I⁻—and susceptibility to phase segregation under thermal stress; these instabilities are mitigated by precise crystallization control enabled by the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration, which balances nucleation density and growth kinetics, while the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent expulsion) establishes a transient supersaturation window that—when precisely interrupted at 6 s into the high-speed step with 220 µL of antisolvent—triggers instantaneous, homogeneous nucleation across the substrate, suppressing Ostwald ripening and yielding uniform, pinhole-free grains with reduced interfacial trap states; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min drives complete DMSO/PbI₂ adduct decomposition, promotes crystallographic relaxation, and eliminates residual strain—as corroborated by XRD showing sharp, narrow (001) and (110) peaks without detectable PbI₂ residuals at ~12.6° or δ-phase impurities—thereby enhancing carrier diffusion length and reducing non-radiative recombination pathways; the resulting film morphology, confirmed by optical imaging, exhibits >98% surface coverage with grayscale intensity homogeneity <5% RSD and negligible dark-spot density in PL mapping, directly evidencing suppressed spatial heterogeneity in defect distribution and continuity of charge transport pathways; concurrently, the high-intensity, monoexponential PL decay with τ₁ ≈ 320 ns and minimal fast-decaying component (<5% amplitude) reflects effective suppression of shallow and deep traps at grain boundaries and surfaces, consistent with both structural ordering and interfacial passivation; collectively, these crystallization-optimized morphological, optical, and structural attributes synergistically elevate charge extraction efficiency, minimize voltage losses from interfacial recombination, and maximize photocurrent generation and fill factor, yielding VOC = 1.138 V, JSC = 21.168 mA/cm², FF = 70.0905%, and PCE = 16.8841%.
